questions.question:
Seven boxes, B, D, E, P, S, T and W, are kept one over the other, but not necessarily in the same order.

W is kept immediately above T. D is kept immediately above S. Only P is kept above B. Only two boxes are kept above W. D is not kept at the third position from the bottom.

How many boxes are kept between E and P?
questions.solution:
Given: Seven boxes, B, D, E, P, S, T and W, are kept one over the other, but not necessarily in the same order.

1) Only P is kept above B.

2) Only two boxes are kept above W.

3) W is kept immediately above T.

 
 

 Boxes
 
 

 P
 
 

 B
 
 

 W
 
 

 T
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 

4) D is kept immediately above S.

5) D is not kept at the third position from the bottom.

The remaining position will be occupied by the only box left i.e. E. 

 
 

 Boxes
 
 

 P
 
 

 B
 
 

 W
 
 

 T
 
 

 E
 
 

 D
 
 

 S
 
 

Thus, three boxes are kept between E and P.

Hence, "Option 3" is the correct answer.

(Left) £ $ 9 3 4 9 7 £ % & # 7 3 1 8 7 5 * @ 4 £ $ (Right)

How many such numbers are there, each of which is immediately preceded by a symbol and also immediately followed by a symbol?
questions.solution:
Given series: (Left) £ $ 9 3 4 9 7 £ % & # 7 3 1 8 7 5 * @ 4 £ $ (Right)

According to the question:

Required condition: Symbol - Number - Symbol

(Left) £ $ 9 3 4 9 7 £ % & # 7 3 1 8 7 5 * __**@ 4 £**__ $ (Right)

Thus, there is one such number which is immediately preceded by a symbol and also immediately followed by a symbol.

Hence, "Option 3" is the correct answer.

questions.solution:

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding to/subtracting from/multiplying with 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(10, 150, 5)

(8, 96, 4)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

(10, 150, 5) → 10 × 5 × 3 = 150

And,

(8, 96, 4) → 8 × 4 × 3 = 96

Similarly,

(9, 162, 6) → 9 × 6 × 3 = 162

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.

questions.question: Abhishek ranked 17th from the top and 49th from the bottom in his class. How many students are there in his class?
questions.solution:
Given:

Abhishek's rank from the top → 17

Abhishek's rank from the bottom → 49

Total students → Abhishek's rank from the top + Abhishek's rank from the bottom - 1

​→ 17 + 49 - 1 = 65

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

This question is based on the five, three-digit numbers given below.

(Left) 715, 906, 570, 853, 418 (Right)

(Example- 697 – First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7)

NOTE - All operations to be done from left to right.

What will be the resultant if the third digit of the highest number is added to the second digit of the lowest number?
questions.solution:
Given series: (Left) 715, 906, 570, 853, 418 (Right)

According to the question.

 
 

 Given
 715
 906
 570
 853
 418
 
 

 Arranged in ascending order
 418
 570
 715
 853
 906
 
 

So,

Third digit of the highest number → 90__**6**__ → 6

Second digit of the lowest number → 4__**1**__8 → 1

So, the third digit of the highest number is added to the second digit of the lowest number → 6 + 1 = 7

Hence, "Option 4" is the correct answer.

Thus, three people sit between A and C when counted from the right of C.

Hence, "Option 1" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All eggs are artists.

Some mangoes are artists.

**Conclusions:**

(I): Some eggs are mangoes.

(II): Some artists are eggs.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fd4563072a4787d5658ac2da823dcbf987cae81f97f2572720758c2b0b38f10a.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) Some eggs are mangoes → **Does not** follow (As all eggs are artists and some mangoes are artists. So it is possible but not definite.)

(II) Some artists are eggs → Follow (As all eggs are artists. As whole eggs comes in artists, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion (II) follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

All cobras are mats.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".
